body.translated_text:
Composed by the venerable teacher <s>Nāgārjuna</s>:
<s>Āryadharmadhātugarbhavivaraṇa</s> (A Commentary on the Noble Essence of the Realm of Truth)

In the Indian language: <s>Āryadharmadhātugarbhavivaraṇa</s>.
In the Tibetan language: 'phags pa chos kyi dbyings kyi snying po'i rnam par bshad pa.

children.text: ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetuṃ teṣāṃ tathāgato hyavadat |
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>dharmas</s> arise from causes — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has indeed declared their cause.

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃvādī mahāśramaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And their cessation — thus proclaims the <s>Mahāśramaṇa</s> (Great Ascetic).

body.text:
ityuktam |
atra 'ye dharmā' iti saptabhiḥ prakārairavagantavyāḥ | tadyathā- vijñānaṃ nāmarūpaṃ ṣaḍāyatanaṃ sparśaḥ vedanā jātirjarāmaraṇamiti | ime dharmāḥ api pañcabhyaḥ prakārebhya utpadyanta iti 'hetuprabhavāḥ' ityuktam | ke te pañca hetavaḥ? avidyā tṛṣṇā upādānaṃ saṃskārā bhavaśceti |
body.translated_text: Thus it is said. Here, 'whatever <s>dharmas</s>' are to be understood in seven aspects, namely: <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form), <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (the six sense-bases), <s>sparśa</s> (contact), <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>jāti</s> (birth), and <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (old age and death). These <s>dharmas</s> arise from five types (of causes), hence it is said 'arising from causes' (<s>hetuprabhavāḥ</s>). What are those five causes? <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), <s>upādāna</s> (grasping), <s>saṃskārāḥ</s> (volitional formations), and <s>bhava</s> (becoming).

body.text: saptavidhānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ pañcaprakārāṇāṃ ca teṣāṃ hetūnāṃ nirodhastāvad 'hetuṃ teṣāṃ ca yo nirodhaḥ' ityādinābhihitaḥ | sa evopaśamaḥ mokṣo nirvāṇamiti | sa ca kenoktaḥ? 'tathāgato hyavadat | iti | tenopadiṣṭa ityabhiprāyeṇa tathā kathitam |
body.translated_text: The cessation of the seven kinds of <s>dharmas</s> and of their five kinds of causes is expressed by 'their cause and their cessation' and so forth. That very (cessation) is quiescence, liberation, <s>nirvāṇa</s>. And by whom was it declared? 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> has indeed declared' — the intended meaning is that it was taught by him. Thus it is stated.

body.text: arthānāṃ yathā sthitistathā (yathāvat) avabodhāt 'tathāgataḥ' ityucyate | vastūnāṃ yathā sthitiḥ, tasyā abhrāntatayā anyebhyo deśanād vā 'tathāgataḥ' | evaṃvidho yo deśakaḥ, yaścaivaṃ svayaṃ bodhakaḥ śravaṇaśīlayuktaśca sa 'evaṃvādī' (mahāśramaṇaḥ) ityuktaḥ |
body.translated_text: Because of awakening to things as they truly are (<s>yathāvat</s>), (he) is called '<s>Tathāgata</s>' (thus-come). Or, because of teaching others the true nature of things without error, (he is called) '<s>Tathāgata</s>.' Such a teacher, and one who himself thus awakens and is endowed with the discipline of listening — he is called '<s>evaṃvādī mahāśramaṇaḥ</s>' (the Great Ascetic who speaks thus).

body.text: 'mahān'-śabdaḥ pradhāna-adbhutaparamapravaraparyāyaḥ | yo vādī vidvān vīraḥ tapasvī mahotsāhaḥ tīvravīryaḥ adbhutakarmakāri ca bhavati, sa eva 'mahān' iti | (sa) aśeṣajñātavyānāṃ jñānād 'vidvān' | aśeṣakleśānāṃ damane samarthatvād 'vīraḥ' | śīlasya samyagbhāvanayā 'tapasvī' | guṇādiṣvaparikhedād 'mahotsāhaḥ' | yasya śiraḥ kapālaṃ vā agninā dīptam, tadavān iva 'tīvravīryaḥ tathā adbhutadharmāṇāṃ sākṣātkāritvād 'adbhutakarmakārī' iti | etādṛśa eva 'mahān' ityucyate |
body.translated_text: The word '<s>mahān</s>' (great) is a synonym for supreme, wonderful, paramount, and most excellent. One who is a speaker, learned, heroic, ascetic, of great zeal, of fierce effort, and a worker of marvels — he alone is called 'great.' He is 'learned' (<s>vidvān</s>) because of knowing all that is to be known. He is 'heroic' (<s>vīra</s>) because of being capable of taming all afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>). He is 'ascetic' (<s>tapasvī</s>) because of the proper cultivation of moral discipline (<s>śīla</s>). He is 'of great zeal' (<s>mahotsāha</s>) because of being untiring in virtues and the like. He is 'of fierce effort' (<s>tīvravīrya</s>) as if one whose head or skull were ablaze with fire. And he is 'a worker of marvels' (<s>adbhutakarmakārī</s>) because of directly realizing wondrous <s>dharmas</s>. One who is exactly such is called 'great.'

body.text: śramaṇaḥ iti pāpānāṃ kleśānāṃ copaśamād 'śramaṇaḥ' | sarvapāpānāṃ prakṣālanād 'brāhmaṇaḥ' | kleśaklamathaparivarjanād 'śramaṇaḥ' svakīyamalāpasāraṇāt 'pravrajitaḥ' iti | ityevaṃvidhairguṇaiḥ samanvāgata iti | bhagavatā buddhenokta ityanena yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | evameva duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgasatyeṣvapi yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ |
body.translated_text: '<s>Śramaṇa</s>' (ascetic): he is a '<s>śramaṇa</s>' because of the pacification of sins and afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>). He is a '<s>brāhmaṇa</s>' because of washing away all sins. He is a '<s>śramaṇa</s>' because of abandoning the fatigue of afflictions. He is a '<s>pravrajita</s>' (renunciant) because of removing his own impurities. Thus, he is endowed with such qualities. The connection should be made with: 'spoken by the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>.' In the same way, the connection should be made with the truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path (<s>duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgasatya</s>).

body.text: avidyāhetoḥ saṃskārāḥ, ityārabhya jarāmaraṇaparyantaṃ (svabhāvataḥ siddhaṃ) kartāramanapekṣya samutpādastāvad 'anulomaḥ' | avidyādihetūnāṃ nivṛtteravabodhaḥ 'pratilomaḥ' ityuktaḥ |
body.translated_text: From the cause of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) arise <s>saṃskārāḥ</s> (volitional formations) — beginning thus and extending up to <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (old age and death), arising without depending on an (inherently existent) creator is called the 'forward order' (<s>anuloma</s>). The understanding of the cessation of causes beginning with <s>avidyā</s> is called the 'reverse order' (<s>pratiloma</s>).

body.text: avidyānivṛtteḥ saṃskārādayo nivartanta ityupadeśakārakatvāt (bhagavān buddha eva) 'mahāśramaṇaḥ' iti |
body.translated_text: Because he instructs that from the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>saṃskārāḥ</s> (volitional formations) and the rest cease, (the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>) is called the '<s>Mahāśramaṇa</s>' (Great Ascetic).
The '<s>Āryadharmadhātugarbhavivaraṇa</s>' (Commentary on the Noble Essence of the Realm of Truth), composed by the venerable teacher <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, is completed.

body.text: bhāratīyopādhyāyena jñānagarbheṇa 'mahālocāvā vande palacekmahābhāgena cānūdya saṃśodhya ca sunirṇītam |
body.translated_text: By the Indian scholar (<s>upādhyāya</s>) <s>Jñānagarbha</s>, together with the great fortunate translator, it was translated, corrected, and well-established.
